The observation that must land first is THIS LANE'S OWN WORK OBJECT. WO-20260909-NO-DETECTOR-CAN-SEE-A-POSITION-MISSING-FROM-THE-VENUE-LIST.yaml is not on origin/main (eight other WO-20260909-* objects are), so the contract this diff would be judged against does not exist yet and I was instructed to wait for it rather than reconstruct it from the spawn prompt. Until it lands I cannot verify this diff satisfies its four done_condition clauses -- and I already know clause (3) is unsatisfiable as written, since it requires observing the detector report the bybit_2/ETHUSDT known positive and MI-221 established that no repo surface can see that position at all.

The second reason is the substantive one. The diff itself is unambiguously Tier-1 -- 10 passing characterization tests, one evidence doc, one DOCUMENT-INDEX row, no src/, no config/, no deploy/, no .github/workflows/, no order path -- and by .github/pr-landing/README.md's own routing it would qualify for landing: self. It declares hold anyway because its SUBSTANCE is a direction change: this lane was spawned to BUILD a roster-driven position sweep, and the finding is that the sweep already exists inside account_open_positions (clients.py:1410, from BL-20260713), already ran on bybit_2/ETHUSDT, and returned nothing -- so building it would have shipped a duplicate that reports the target position CLEAN, which is the blind detector the object forbids. Declining to build the directed thing is the manager's call to ratify, not mine to take unilaterally, and landing the evidence doc that asserts it would take it.

Handing to the manager, session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj. On their word this flips to landing: self and arms in one push with the merge_slot claim per R13. Auto-merge is NOT armed by this branch (R10 clean). Remediation for the real gap -- _emit's 'if size <= 0: return' collapsing venue-flat / zero-size-row / no-row into one value -- is deliberately NOT in this diff: that return value feeds a live real-money close decision at order_monitor.py:4348, making it Tier-2/3, and MI-221 explicitly HELD it for the same reason. No order was placed, modified or cancelled on any account; every venue fact in this diff is cited from MI-221's GETs or read from source.
why:
Tier-1 by the canonical doc's own list, and I want to be precise about why rather than leaning on the path list. The whole diff is: one new test file (tests/test_accounts_clients_position_read_state_collapse.py, 10 characterization tests, all passing), one evidence doc under docs/claude/work/, one hand-written row in docs/DOCUMENT-INDEX.md, and the two relay request files that open and hold this PR. There is no src/, no config/, no deploy/, no .github/workflows/, no strategy params, no risk caps, no order path, and no runtime code of any kind -- nothing in this diff executes on the live VM.

The tests are characterization tests: they pin CURRENT behaviour of clients.py::account_open_positions, they do not change it. That distinction is what keeps this Tier-1 rather than Tier-2. The defect they document -- _emit's 'if size <= 0: return' collapsing three venue states into one indistinguishable value, and its symbol-dedupe dropping a second live hedge book -- sits on a live real-money close decision (order_monitor.py:4348), so FIXING it is Tier-2/3. I have deliberately not fixed it; MI-221 reached the same boundary and HELD for the same reason. Writing the defect down and making it executable is Tier-1 work; changing what the reconciler considers open is not, and I have not done the second thing.

DOCUMENT-INDEX.md was edited BY HAND rather than via scripts/ops/document_index.py --write, matching MI-221's precedent, because that script rewrites hundreds of files and bumps a canonical doc's last-verified date, fabricating an attestation nobody made.

Guards run in-session: check_document_index.py OK (population 1031, registered 1031), check_canonical_doc_coherence.py all checks passed, ruff clean on the new file, and 32 tests green (my 10 plus the 22 existing in the sibling file test_accounts_clients_open_positions.py, run together to prove I did not break the file I am extending). tests/test_diag_exchange_positions.py could NOT be run here -- fastapi is absent from this container -- so I am stating that as unrun rather than implying full coverage; it is untouched by this diff and CI covers it.
